c03_chuqui.jpg.desc: Panoramic view of Chuquicamata, a state-owned copper mine located at 2,850 metres (9,350 ft) above sea level just outside Calama, north of Chile. It is by excavated volume the largest open pit copper mine in the world. The huge hole was started in 1882 as a mine to extract gold and copper. It is 4.5 kilometres (2.8 mi) long, 3.5 kilometres (2.2 mi) wide and with a depth of 850 metres (2,790 ft) it is the second deepest open-pit mine in the world (after Bingham Canyon Mine in Utah, USA). Note: to get a feeling of the scale spot out a haul truck, which is 9.5 metres (31 ft) long and 4.5 metres (15 ft) high.
c03_chuqui.jpg.title: File:Mina de Chuquicamata, Calama, Chile, 2016-02-01, DD 110-112 PAN.JPG

ma_desupreme.jpg.desc: Built in 1909, this Colonial Revival-style building was originally designed by Edward L. Tilton as an addition to the Old Delaware State House, doubling the size of the old capitol, and was heavily renovated to its present appearance in 1968. The building is clad in red flemish bond brick with a hipped roof, a cornice with dentils, fifteen-over-fifteen and nine-over-nine double-hung windows, a one-story north wing with a semi-circular portico, a rear wing with arched bays, and a decorative trim surround and fanlight transom at the main entrance bay. The building is a contributing structure in the Dover Green Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977. The building today houses the Delaware Supreme Court.
ma_desupreme.jpg.title: File:Delaware Supreme Court Building, The Green, Dover, DE.jpg
